text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000208 bills 99215 far above expectation, mostly on low-complexity patients, but the returned charts fully support the billed levels while showing signs of templated or inflated notes.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern looks like upcoding: 99215 use is elevated in every complexity stratum, not just among sicker patients, and sampled low-complexity 99215s carry routine diagnoses such as upper respiratory infection (C0101102, C0101238), UTI (C0101277) and follow-up visits (C0101101). The records review points the other way, with no documented 99215 falling below the billed level against a substantial all-provider mismatch rate. That level of agreement is unusually clean given normal documentation noise, and the note checks suggest the charts may be built to match the bill rather than the visit. Signs include repeated time entries, duplicate content, late notes (including supported 99215 C0101315) and moderate-or-higher data reviewed on claims with no lab or test line, though each is only weak evidence. Documentation covers only about 8% of claims and no audit trail was received, so a reviewer should first request audit logs and compare note text across the documented low-complexity 99215s to check for cloning before treating the documentation as genuine support."}
